title: hire-grpc exports types from tonic and sibling crates without re-exporting them
description:
rust.md: "If crate `A`'s public API uses types that are defined in crate `B`, but does not re-export crate `B`, then `A` updating its dependency on `B` must be considered a semver-breaking change to `A`."

hire-grpc's public API uses, and does not re-export:
- `tonic::Status` and `tonic::Request`/`Response` — throughout hire-grpc/src/service.rs, and unavoidably in the generated `workload` module (lib.rs:8-10)
- `hire_core::SvidSigner` and `hire_core::TrustBundleStore` — service.rs:17-18, in `WorkloadApiService`'s public fields and `new()` signature
- `hire_attestors::Attestor` — service.rs:19, same

hire-grpc/src/lib.rs:1-10 contains only `pub mod` declarations; there is no `pub use` of any dependency.

The tonic case is the one that bites. tonic is at 0.12, still pre-1.0, and bumps its public types on every minor release — it is not in the "widely-used ecosystem staple you need not re-export" category that rust.md carves out for tokio and serde. Downstream code today has to add its own `tonic = "0.12"` dependency and keep the version in lockstep by hand; when hire-grpc moves to tonic 0.13, every consumer breaks with a type mismatch on `Status` and no version bump of hire-grpc signals it.

hire-core and hire-attestors are path dependencies inside this workspace, so they are lower risk, but re-exporting them (`pub use hire_core;`) removes the need for consumers to depend on them directly just to name `SvidSigner`.

Fix: `pub use tonic;` plus `pub use hire_attestors;` / `pub use hire_core;` in hire-grpc/src/lib.rs.
